- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off or market uncertainty.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after 80+ from peak), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 3–5 days post-peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; use 7-day rolling average to dampen noise.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.33, 1.00), model may misalign with trend; align forecast to sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses direction; use sentiment as signal to adjust slope (e.g., +0.5% if sentiment >0.67, -0.5% if <0.33).
